findings.text: The boundary-flux reference is case["analytic_read"].boundary_flux, and analytic_read is topology.read on the analytic flux (scripts/prototypes/tracked_read/measure.py build_kind), i.e. the present read the plan replaces; sub-millisecond-forward-path section 2 requires both references to be located by a direct Newton solve on the analytic psi so that no read instrument decides its own clause, so the boundary clause is judged against read code rather than against an independent reference.

The accuracy gate is committed red at head (3 failing ids, EXIT=1) and section 2's accuracy clause is therefore unmet; the manifest records this under outside_scope and attributes the error to the trial booking and the Bell interpolant upstream of support_read, and the coordinator must decide whether that attribution stands.

No test fails if the single-owner property regresses: restoring support_read.stationary_cells, or inlining the argmin back into BellField.value, leaves tests/test_tracked_read.py green because it passes 4 of 4 at the base as well as the head, so the done-when's own gate cannot distinguish the two revisions and the reuse removal is evidenced only by reading the diff.

The four committed job scripts hardcode this run's absolute instance directory, including the run id, in #SBATCH --output and RUN=, so none of them runs for anyone else and a run identifier is carried into the repository.

The H200 wall table reads as this node's own measurement but both measuring jobs (logs/h200_1299299.log, logs/h200_1299301.log) ran at the base revision a1f6782 and no log line or table caption names a revision, and section 2 asks for the warm wall by stage at base and at head, so no head-arm wall exists.
The cited accuracy-gate log carries no device label, contrary to the brief's fourth item, although its enclosing job log logs/accuracy_1299308.log does read '# device NVIDIA H200 NVL'.
The commits list omits e11c1149c and the reviewed head 2e007b43d, and changed_paths and artifacts cite two PNG twins that the head deletes, so the record is stale against the tree it describes.
